## Introduction

For this Project, I will be tidying three different data sources.

- WHO Tuberculosis Cases
  - This dataset is built directly into the tidyr package and it is a great example of where column names are encoded with data values.
- World Bank Labor Data
  - I used the World Bank's "[DataBank](https://databank.worldbank.org/source/jobs/Type/TABLE/preview/on#)" tool to download multiple labor statistics about different countries.
- Wikipedia List of Countries by Electricity Production
  - This data source is a list of energy production by country, and will give me great practice in scrapping an HTML table from the web.

## Approach

### WHO Tuberculosis Cases

This dataset is a classic example of a dataset that needs to be tidy. I will have to turn the column names into values, and then do some basic exploratory data analysis.

### World Bank Labor Data

In this dataset, I will need to turn the year columns into one with year values. As well, I will need to make separate tables for countries, series, and wage data points. This is to make the tables normalized.

### Wikipedia List of Countries by Electricity Production

This dataset will be the most complicated because it was read directly from Wikipedia and has some errors. I will need to turn the energy production methods into one column, and have another column to keep the renewable / fossil fuel hierarchy.

## Code

```{R Libraries}
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rvest)
```

Below I loaded the data sets I will be analyzing. The WHO and wage stats data were easily to load, but I was able to practice web strapping with the Wikipedia data. I used the rvest library, and read the all the HMTL tables to a vector in R. I knew from the website that I wanted the first table, so I pulled out the table at position 1.

```{R Loading Data}

#Dataset 1
who_data <- who

#Dataset 2
wage_data <- read.csv("wage_stats.csv")

#Dataset 3
url <- "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_electricity_production"

tables <- url |>
  read_html() |>
  html_table(fill=TRUE)

electricity_data <- tables[[1]]

write.csv(electricity_data,"wiki_prod_electricity.csv")
```
